rationale: I went and looked, at the size the thing actually ships at. shots/mgr105-1200-day.png, seed 42, day 4 10:36, clear early summer: the town above the lane is dense and finished, and the bottom fifth of the picture is dead. Two separate faults, both in the band #100 built, and I measured both on HEAD rather than guessing. (1) The black bar under the picture is not the apron and not unpainted canvas - it is drawSill() itself, filling #0a0806 flat over the strip below sillTop(). Sampled below sillTop at three viewports and three hours, min luma == max luma == mean, exactly: 8.4 by day, 6.2 at dusk, 3.0 at night, zero pixels above luma 20 in 42,624 / 62,628 / 6,358. The sill's lit front edge, its two geranium pots and its cup are silhouetted in rgba(9,8,6) against a #0a0806 ground - under one luma unit of contrast. The whole framing conceit of the piece, the thing the fourth domain is named after, renders as a bar. That is b105. (2) Directly above it, the near roof is the largest single object in the frame (13.8% of a desktop picture, 21.7% of a phone, per #100) and NOTHING LIVES ON IT - not by oversight but by construction: the bed CA, the item sort, the seed scatter and every spawner bound their y loops at LN_WALK_S 79, and catA is pinned to the lane at x -2..66. It has a ridge, two light wells, a dormer per house, party walls, stacks and moss, and no tenant. That is b106, the bet, and it is where c151 has been pointing since #99. The rest balance the grid on cues that a worker already measured and that name their own fix: b107 takes c143 and c152 together, because both reduce to one thing (#101's own words - a far-end stay that clears by 03h needs an EARLIER far-side source, not better pricing), and it is the third pass those two have survived; b108 is c142's thin gardener in the courtyard, 9 back and the title object; b109 is c146's dawn re-key, small but sitting on the morning lapse hour that is one tap away. This is RUNG 2 and I am calling it that rather than dressing it up: the frontier right now is genuinely a deepen, the two spatial and structural rungs were spent at #99 (4b) and #94 (6), and the ladder's own note is that rung 2 is usually the highest-yield move. It is the first rung<=2 pass in three, so the rule is not binding - but it binds the next one, and if the batch after this also wants rung 2 it must climb instead. On memory: budget was OVER 13 opens running and three workers wrote to me about it. I distilled rather than deferred - LAWS 25 laws/12.0 KB -> 18 laws/12.0 KB (promoted #100-#104's six laws by MERGING them into their subjects rather than stacking; cut 'The sill is DOM' outright, folding its one live clause into the camera law; merged the two anchor laws, the two probe/instant laws, the two counting laws, and #102's + #104's judging-a-look laws into one). Inventory 11.6 -> 8.3 KB as nouns plus one primary seam each, with three factual corrections: the near roof is no longer VOID, the sill's paint is now recorded, and 'nothing living goes south of LN_WALK_S' is now written down instead of being rediscovered. Cues 10 -> 3: seven closed, five of them because they are briefs in this queue. And I found the mechanism behind the drift - the protocol says promoted Law:/Cue: lines are cut from the entry once the manager has promoted them, and no pass had ever done it; doing it took the ledger tail 9.8 -> 8.1 KB on its own.

queue.brief: The bottom band of every frame is a flat black bar, and it is drawn on purpose by drawSill(). Measured on HEAD this pass, seed 42 simT 175 (day 4, 10:36, daylight 0.90), deviceScaleFactor 1: sampling the canvas below sillTop(), min luma == max luma == mean == 8.4 at 1200x720, 1600x950 AND 390x844 - a perfectly uniform fill, 0 pixels above luma 20 out of 42,624 / 62,628 / 6,358. At daylight 0.37 it is 6.2 flat; at 0.00, 3.0 flat. The strip is max(26, H*0.075), 5.8-7.2% of every frame. drawSill's own features - a 2.2 px lit front edge, two geranium pots and a cup at 5.5% and 94.5% of W - are silhouetted in rgba(9,8,6) against a #0a0806 ground, under one luma unit apart, so the sill this whole domain is named after cannot be seen. Above it the apron compounds the problem at small sizes: at 1600x950 its gradient ramps 123-109-99-89-82 and then cliffs to 8, but at 1200x720 that ramp is one row (119 -> 45 -> 8), so the near roof reads as a thin grey strip over a black bar. Make the bottom band read as a windowsill in shadow - a surface with a near edge, some depth, and something standing on it. Note drawSill runs inside drawOurSide, which runs inside drawGround: it is baked into the GROUND CACHE, so anything per-frame there has to be a live overlay.
queue.successLooksLike: At 1200x720 DSF1, seed 42 t=175, the strip below sillTop() has an internal luma RANGE of at least 12 where HEAD's is exactly 0.0, and the pots and cup are findable in a difference image against HEAD. The band still reads clearly darker than the roof above it at every hour you sample, and the roof-apron-sill transition is a gradient rather than a cliff at 1200x720.
queue.avoid: Do NOT just raise the brightness. #100's finding stands and is why the band is dark: a dark near block is what lets the town read past it. The fix is value SEPARATION inside a dark band - a real dark surface still shows 15-30 luma of internal range - not a higher mean. Do not change sillTop()'s formula without checking viewFor(), which reads it as the ONE definition and prices the camera against it.

queue.brief: THE BET - take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. #100 gave the diorama a foreground and it is now the largest single object in the frame (13.8% of a 1600x950 picture, 21.7% of a 390x844 phone, measured there). Nothing lives on it, and not by oversight: grep confirms the bed CA, the item sort and the opening seed scatter all bound their y loops at LN_WALK_S (79), and catA is pinned to the lane at y = LANE_N_Y - 0.5, x -2..66. So the near roof - rows 79..WH, with a capped ridge, two WELLS, a dormer or rooflight per house at DORM_Y 85, party walls with stacks at STACK_Y 86, a parapet at PARA_Y and moss on the north pitch - has no inhabitants of any kind. Give it its own life. The town already has the tenants: birds[] land/hop/fly, and plazaBirdSpot() is the model to copy - a place-specific spot picker with its OWN roll and cap, which is exactly how #92 stopped the plaza's pigeons competing for a shared budget. catA is the second: a cat that has only ever walked the lane could come up onto the parapet after dark and walk the ridge, which is the nearest and largest thing in the night picture. MUR_ROOSTS could take a near-roof entry. And c151's other half is still open: nothing looks down the two light wells.
queue.successLooksLike: On a wide shot at 1200x720 the near roof is somewhere the eye goes: at least one living thing is on it in a clear majority of daylit samples, counted by its own probe against a HEAD control that reads zero, and after dark the cat or a roosting bird is findable in the same band. The roof stops being the emptiest surface in the picture.
queue.avoid: Do not widen the general birds[] roll or spawnLaneAgent to reach the roof - a spawn band is a share of a budget, so the roof needs its own source and its own cap (plazaBirdSpot is the pattern). Do not put PEOPLE on it. Do not move LN_WALK_S or change the near block's footprint: #100's roof is emergent from buildVolumes and a footprint change grows a different roof. Two traps that will bite: project() lifts z NORTHWARD ~1.15 rows per cell of height, so a bird on the ridge at row 83 can render north of the lane - price everything by its own row exactly as #100 had to for the stacks; and drawNearRoof is in the GROUND CACHE, so anything that moves must be a live overlay after the cache blit, and anything warm at night must go in a screen pass AFTER applyLight.

queue.brief: The far side has no source that puts anybody on it in the morning, and two open cues are the same fault seen twice. c143 (#96): the punt runs at ~zero because jetty stands are ALL 17:30-03:00 against an eastOpen() close of 20.6, so nothing fits. c152 (#101, measured over 248 far-side retirements): the deck's far posts are 33 cells / 4.7 h at a hurry from EAST_GATE_A and their source releases nobody before sunDown-4, so arrivals sit at sunDown+1.8 median. #101's own conclusion, after trying the other lever: a far-end stay that clears by 03h needs an EARLIER far-side source, not better pricing. spawnEastAgent is the only source out there and it opens late. Give the far bank its own arrival source with a morning-side window - people who come to the church, the orchard, the towpath or the mill early - so the punt has a rider that fits and the deck's far posts can be occupied and cleared before the night. This is the third manager pass these two cues have survived; they are a brief now or a deletion.
queue.successLooksLike: On a fine summer day the far bank has people on it before noon where HEAD has none - show the HEAD zero first, since that is the whole premise. The punt makes at least one crossing on a majority of fine days, counted over 10 seeds. And no more nights hold a dusk agent at 03:00 than HEAD's 4 of 40.
queue.avoid: Do NOT re-price stayOn at the choice: #101 measured that and it takes far-post fits from 41 in 248 to 2, deleting #85's stay outright. queue.brief: The courtyard is the title object and has been untouched since #95, the longest gap in the town, and the person who tends it is nearly never there. Measured at #94: gardener presence is a 13 h mean of 0.17 in summer, 0 in winter, and above zero in only 5 of 30 samples - despite 0.7 set-outs a day. The cause named at #95 is a one-at-a-time rule plus long walks, and the fix it suggested is a gardener who arrives EARLY (a sunrise set-out through a short door) or a second bed slot. Make the courtyard visibly tended: someone in it, working, for a real share of the daylight.
queue.successLooksLike: Summer gardener presence over 13 h rises materially above HEAD's 0.17 mean and winter stops being a flat zero, reported for HEAD and candidate from the same probe on the same seeds. Measure PRESENCE over folded time, not a per-instant crop.
queue.avoid: Do not add a new kind of worker, and do not raise the set-out rate - 0.7/day is already fine and the fault is presence, not arrivals. Price presence as rate x visit before you touch any cap: lengthen the stay or shorten the walk. Do not let a longer stay block the bed the way the one-at-a-time rule already does; release the bed as the walk out begins.

queue.brief: The town's windows light UP as the sun rises, which is backwards. Measured at #94 with probes/dawn-lit.mjs: windowLit's early risers key on the dawn EDGE at sunUp+1.3..2.1 h, so lit panes RISE after sunrise - 5 at dawn to 11 at sunUp+0.5 in winter. #98's named fix is to re-key hRise to sunUp-0.8..+0.4, so panes are lit BEFORE first light and go out as the town wakes. Small, but it sits on the morning: the clock button's second tap lands at sunUp+0.5 (watch note), which makes this the hour a visitor is most likely to look at after touching anything.
queue.successLooksLike: At sunUp+0.5 in winter the count of lit panes is FALLING, not rising. Print the HEAD and candidate curves across the year from probes/dawn-lit.mjs, and show the evening curve is unchanged.
queue.avoid: Do not touch the evening half of windowLit - it is tuned and the LIT_PANES night composite from #61/#93 depends on it. Do not add a morning source; the morning's population is b107's and b108's territory, not this brief's. Remember the hour of the sun is solved at the ARRIVAL instant: fixed-point any sunUp read on sunAt(t) rather than a stale value.
